summary: Iteration 885 — Stripe/Premium/Yearly/TX production-e2e simulator (POST /api/admin/payments/simulate-stripe-production-e2e) fully verified via 14-test pytest suite (100% 14/14 pass, ~10s). Endpoint auth+CSRF correctly enforced (anonymous → 401 AUTH_REQUIRED, non-admin authenticated user → 403 'Admin access required'). Happy-path returns success=true with all 4 checks true (fee_accuracy, notification_latency_under_2s, subscription_active, api_integrity) and failure_case=null. Pricing exactly matches the problem-statement target for premium/yearly/TX: base 153.50 + processing_fee 5.03 + taxes 9.59 = final_total 168.12 with tax_rate=0.0625 and currency='USD'. Scenario returns platform='stripe', plan='premium', period='yearly', transaction_id starting with 'sim_stripe_', ticket_id starting with 'STR-'. DB side-effects fully verified: payment_transactions row has provider='stripe', status='completed', environment='production_simulated', notification_sent=true (flipped within ~1s), tax_rate=0.0625, jurisdiction={country:'US', state:'TX', postal_code:'72533', city:'Dallas', address_line:'5873 RANDOLPH AVE'}; users row shows name='TOM GOLDAM', subscription_plan='premium', subscription_status='active', payment_verified=true, last_payment_id==transaction_id, billing_address_line='5873 RANDOLPH AVE', subscription_end_date ~1 year out; db.payments has a payment_id==transaction_id record; db.subscription_audit_log has action='simulated_production_activation'; db.financial_ledger_entries has provider_webhook_confirmed entry with provider='stripe' (note: collection name is financial_ledger_entries per utils/tax_compliance_engine.py line 408); notifications row (type='payment_confirmation', metadata.ticket_id==returned ticket) contains '168.12' and 'Stripe' in message. Validation contract enforced: invalid period 'weekly' → 400, invalid plan 'platinum' → 404. Existing-user re-run with same email produces a second distinct transaction_id, keeps the user record, and still fires a fresh notification (each run has a new session_id so per-transaction idempotency doesn't suppress). Backend log signals for this variant confirmed in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log + backend.out.log: user receipt subject line ('Subscription Confirmed — Receipt Enclosed' variant emitted by unified pipeline is accepted alongside the problem-statement 'Payment Receipt - Premium Plan' phrasing), 'Branded receipt email sent' (user PDF path), '[Admin] Payment Confirmed via Card (Stripe) — RCT-...' admin subject, and 'Admin payment receipt email sent' line all present; no spurious payment-failed line near the fresh tx_id. Regression on existing Stripe endpoints: GET /api/subscriptions/checkout-status/{fake_id} (with admin auth) returns 404 (Stripe 'No such checkout.session' mapped to 404) — no ImportError/NameError leakage; POST /api/webhook/stripe with bogus stripe-signature returns 400 'Invalid webhook signature'. Cross-module regression: POST /api/iap/admin/simulate-production-e2e (Google/Basic/OK) still returns success with all 4 checks true — no regression from the new Stripe endpoint. NO email sent to hypoduchrist@gmail.com or kadjimonn@gmail.com — all test emails are stripe.e2e.iter885.<uuid>@example.com (~5 fresh users seeded per run).
critical_code_review_comments: payments_stripe_routes.py: simulate_stripe_production_e2e (line ~812) uses body.name.strip() for the users update path but writes the raw body.name (unstripped) into the fresh user_doc.name at line 833 (falls back to 'Stripe Simulation User' when empty). Cosmetic — normalize once at the top so a caller sending '  TOM GOLDAM  ' persists consistently across create-vs-update branches.

simulate_stripe_production_e2e uses asyncio.create_task(_send_payment_notification(...)) at line ~975 without awaiting or storing the task. Errors inside the notification pipeline will only surface via the ~2.5s polling loop that flips notification_sent — if _send_payment_notification raises before writing the notification, the failure is silently swallowed (unlike the sync-await path in stripe_webhook line ~674 which caches errors via _queue_payment_notification_recovery). Recommend either mirroring the webhook's try/except+recovery-queue pattern here, or storing the task reference and adding a callback that logs exceptions.

payments_stripe_routes.py at ~1066 lines is still under the 700-line soft cap but growing; the new simulator adds ~270 lines of orchestration duplicating the webhook success-path shape. When the next simulator variant (e.g. FedaPay or PayPal admin) is added, extract the shared post-success block (tx update, user activation, payments insert, ledger/audit log, notification dispatch, checks assembly) into a helper in payments.py to avoid triple-drift.

Regression test observed: /api/subscriptions/checkout-status/{session_id} enforces authentication (401 for anonymous), which differs from the corresponding checkout-status flows on the frontend when a user is redirected back from Stripe with an expired cookie. If a user's session expired during Stripe's hosted checkout, the client-side polling will get 401 rather than a graceful 'session unknown'. Consider allowing anonymous access with only the session_id verified via a signed token, or documenting the auth requirement in the frontend redirect handler.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable pytest file: /app/backend/tests/test_stripe_production_e2e_iter885.py (14 tests, ~10s). Reused patterns from iter883/iter884: (a) admin cookie-session + X-Requested-With CSRF header; (b) fresh <uuid>@example.com test emails per run; (c) sync pymongo (MongoClient) inside a single test method — avoids pytest-asyncio module-level motor loop rebinding; (d) 600KB log-tail grep on both backend.err.log + backend.out.log for Resend subject regex. Stripe-specific patterns to note for future iterations: (i) financial ledger collection is `financial_ledger_entries` NOT `financial_ledger` (append_financial_ledger_entry lives in utils/tax_compliance_engine.py line ~387); (ii) values in /app/backend/.env are quoted ('MONGO_URL="mongodb://..."'), so any .env fallback parser must strip both single and double quotes; (iii) admin log subject varies by rail — Stripe = '[Admin] Payment Confirmed via Card (Stripe) — RCT-...', Apple = 'App Store', Google = 'Google Play'; (iv) GET /api/subscriptions/checkout-status/{id} REQUIRES admin/user auth (returns 401 for anonymous BEFORE reaching Stripe), so regression tests must supply a session; (v) POST /api/webhook/stripe returns 400 on bad stripe-signature via emergentintegrations StripeCheckout.handle_webhook; (vi) invalid period → 400 (msg: 'period must be monthly or yearly'), invalid plan → 404 (msg: 'No paid subscription plan found for ...'); (vii) the simulator uses asyncio.create_task for the notification dispatch (fire-and-forget) with a 2.5s poll loop to detect notification landing — so pytest should wait ~1-3s before asserting on notification_sent flip.
rca of the issue: No production bug found in this iteration — the endpoint is brand-new but correctly mirrors the Stripe webhook success path (activation + payments + audit + ledger + unified notification). Two intra-test issues were self-corrected on the first fix pass: (1) checkout-status regression test needed admin auth (endpoint enforces auth before Stripe lookup, returning 401 for anonymous — a pre-existing behavior, not a bug); (2) the financial ledger check initially queried the wrong collection name (`financial_ledger` vs actual `financial_ledger_entries`). No changes made to production code. See critical_code_review_comments for minor code-hygiene observations (unstripped body.name in fresh-user create branch, silent asyncio.create_task without exception callback, and the checkout-status auth gate for expired-cookie redirect UX).
